frameworks.name: $100 Million Scaling Roadmap
frameworks.definition: A portfolio-derived diagnostic quiz spanning 10 growth stages with prescriptive guidance across 8 business functions (product, marketing, sales, customer success, recruiting, IT, HR, finance) to identify stage-specific constraints and solutions.

claims.text: The primary purpose of publishing the $100 Million Offers book at 99 cents is not revenue generation but maximum distribution to build long-term deal flow for Acquisition.com. Alex Hormozi expects the largest inflow of consulting deals from readers who reach $3-20M revenue within 5 years and become clients seeking $100M scale guidance.
claims.speaker: Alex Hormozi
claims.mechanism: Low-price book distribution maximizes reach; readers who execute and scale become natural high-ticket customers within 5 years when they encounter growth ceiling.
bounded_by: Does not apply to books intended to be primary profit centers
Does not apply to short-term revenue optimization strategies

claims.text: At 99 cents, Amazon's royalty structure gives the platform two-thirds of revenue and the author one-third; at $2.99, the author receives two-thirds and Amazon one-third. The 99-cent price point is selected deliberately to incentivize Amazon's algorithmic promotion and distribution leverage, not to maximize author revenue.
claims.speaker: Alex Hormozi
conditions: goal is maximum reach over maximum author revenue
claims.mechanism: Amazon allocates promotional traffic and algorithmic visibility proportionally to platform profit margin; lower author take at 99 cents aligns incentives with Amazon's distribution engine.

claims.text: There is a psychological difference between a free offer and a paid offer (even at 99 cents): paying for content, however small, converts a person from a casual user into a customer psychologically, increasing commitment and perceived value regardless of price.
claims.speaker: Alex Hormozi
conditions: applies to digital products and educational content
when low price point ($0.99-$2.99) is feasible
claims.mechanism: Payment creates psychological ownership and commitment; the buyer now identifies as a customer (has made a purchase decision) rather than a free-sample consumer.
bounded_by: Does not apply to lead-generation funnels where free is the intended first step before paid upsell
Does not apply when price point is prohibitively high

claims.text: Publishing a value-packed book at ultra-low price (99 cents) distributes the brand to a mass audience and creates a filter mechanism: readers who benefit and act on the content become natural customer prospects 3-5 years later when they encounter scaling constraints that Acquisition.com's services address.
claims.speaker: Alex Hormozi
conditions: services business with 3-5 year customer acquisition horizon
content provides genuine implementation value to readers
claims.mechanism: Low-priced educational content builds authority and reaches a wide base; a percentage of readers execute successfully and later need premium service; initial low price creates reciprocal obligation and brand recall.

numbers.axis: time from book consumption to service purchase

bounded_by: Requires genuinely useful content; low-quality books do not create future customer pipeline
Does not apply to one-time, non-repeatable product categories

claims.text: Giving away the book entirely for free would not have achieved maximum distribution; the 99-cent price point balances Amazon's algorithmic incentives (platform profit share) with customer psychology (ownership via payment) to maximize reach.
claims.speaker: Alex Hormozi
claims.mechanism: Free offerings receive no platform promotional priority (no platform profit to incentivize promotion); paid offerings at low price point create platform profit incentive and customer commitment psychology simultaneously.

examples.text: The listener discovered Hormozi's work through social media visibility, then read the $100 Million Offers book on Audible at 99 cents. The listener's friend group also discovered and consumed the book independently, creating organic word-of-mouth validation. This peer-driven discovery pattern demonstrates the distribution success of the 99-cent price point: the low price removed friction, Amazon's algorithm promoted the book, and readers paid enough to create psychological ownership, resulting in multiple independent social discovery events.

Hormozi created the $100 Million Scaling Roadmap as a free diagnostic quiz that identifies which of 10 growth stages a business occupies and prescribes solutions across 8 functions (product, marketing, sales, customer success, recruiting, IT, HR, finance). The free roadmap serves as a qualification tool: readers who plug in their business data self-identify as relevant prospects (businesses stuck at a specific growth stage), and those who identify as addressable are invited to book a consultation with the Acquisition.com sales team.

practices.text: Publish educational products (books, courses, guides) at ultra-low price points ($0.99-$2.99) on platforms where the distributor receives meaningful revenue share, to align platform incentives with maximum distribution reach.

Create free diagnostic or qualification tools (quizzes, assessments, roadmaps) that ask prospects to self-identify their stage, problem, or fit, converting anonymous audience into a named, qualified lead pool.
Design free lead-generation products around portfolio data and case-study patterns from past customers, using real examples as the primary proof point for the diagnostic tool.
